name: Question 12
worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{yz}{x-2z}) \\  & =-\frac{yz}{(x-2z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-\frac{yz}{(x-2z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{z}{(x-2z)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(-\frac{z}{(x-2z)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{1\cdot (x-2z)^{2}-z\cdot 2(x-2z)\cdot (-2)}{(x-2z)^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{(x-2z)^{2}+4z(x-2z)}{(x-2z)^{4}} \\  & =-\frac{x-2z+4z}{(x-2z)^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{x+2z}{(x-2z)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(1,1,1) & =-\frac{1+2\cdot 1}{(1-2\cdot 1)^{3}}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Evaluate fxyz(1,1,1) for f(x,y,z)=yzx−2z.

a
0
b
1
c
3
d
−1
e
−13
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the first-order derivative fx(x,y,z):

fx(x,y,z)=∂∂x(yzx−2z)=−yz(x−2z)2

Now, we find fxy(x,y,z) by differentiating fx(x,y,z) with respect to y:

fxy(x,y,z)=∂∂y(fx(x,y,z))=∂∂y(−yz(x−2z)2)=−z(x−2z)2

Next, we find fxyz(x,y,z) by differentiating fxy(x,y,z) with respect to z:

fxyz(x,y,z)=∂∂z(fxy(x,y,z))=∂∂z(−z(x−2z)2)=−1⋅(x−2z)2−z⋅2(x−2z)⋅(−2)(x−2z)4=−(x−2z)2+4z(x−2z)(x−2z)4=−x−2z+4z(x−2z)3=−x+2z(x−2z)3

Finally, we evaluate fxyz(x,y,z) at (1,1,1):

fxyz(1,1,1)=−1+2⋅1(1−2⋅1)3=3
